reason: Yes. As the non-sponsor red-teamer, I reviewed the prior digest ad15ec61 and found T12-T25; the sponsor's section 9.2 answers all of them and thirteen changed the text. My decisive objections are fixed: the closed allowlist replaces the open 'predates the token rule' class (T12); 'valid-but-irregular' is replaced by irregular-but-preserved with an operative consequence that the later correction is ineffective (T13); the retrospective statutory breach is reduced to an operational irregularity, so the Act no longer supplies a definition to declare a past statutory breach (T14, T21); the category now has one consequence, a sunset and a Judiciary reliance report (T22); the reviewer is named and must re-derive from the introducing commit (T15, T16); current-cycle, cross-reference, registry fail-closed, marker duty and the seven-test count are fixed (T17-T20, T23, T25). T24 remains a disclosed conflict, not a solved one; I accept it only because T15/T19/T20 make the external checks operational. The Act 22 gate passed as not_exercised because the bill is outside the Clerk-owned pilot; I do not treat that statutory scope exemption as a bar. A yes enacts the prospective anchor rule and the closed legacy remedy; it does not claim the conflict is cured.
